stem: A 55-year-old man of northern European descent has bronze skin, diabetes and knee arthritis. His transferrin saturation and ferritin are both high. His brother and his sister both have diabetes and cirrhosis, and both parents are healthy.
oneliner: 55M northern European + bronze skin, diabetes, arthritis + high transferrin saturation and ferritin + brother and sister with diabetes and cirrhosis, healthy parents → which inheritance pattern?
ask: Which inheritance pattern is most likely?

whyNot.A: Dominant disease needs an **affected parent** in most families; both of his parents are **healthy**
whyNot.C: His **sister** is affected, which would need an **affected father**; both parents are healthy
whyNot.D: Mitochondrial disease passes from an **affected mother**; his **mother is healthy**
whyNot.E: An X-linked dominant disease needs an **affected parent**, and both of his are **healthy**

why: Bronze skin, diabetes, arthritis and **high transferrin saturation and ferritin** point to **hereditary hemochromatosis** (usually HFE C282Y). **Healthy parents with affected siblings of both sexes** fit **autosomal recessive** inheritance.

idea.rule: Healthy parents with affected children of both sexes suggest autosomal recessive inheritance.
